clue.text: "One of theirs" spotted with this in World War II?

definitions.text: "One of theirs" spotted with this in World War II?

parts.words: "One of theirs" spotted with this in World War II?
parts.note: the wartime phrase for an enemy aircraft seen overhead is read as a person covered in spots from an illness named after the enemy nation

explanation.surface: A wartime observer reports sighting one of the enemy's planes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like 'sighted', the plane-spotter's word, but it means covered in spots: the illness is rubella, named after the enemy of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella is the disease commonly called by this name, marked by a red spotty rash.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-well gets no reward for virtue

definitions.meaning: someone whose goodness earns them no return is good for no gain

explanation.surface: A layabout complains that being good never pays.
explanation.definitionFit: A worthless layabout; and literally 'good' with no payment in return.

clue.text: Jovial flagman .

parts.note: jovial means jolly, and the pirate flag called the Jolly one carries a man's name

explanation.surface: A cheerful signalman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jolly Roger is the skull-and-crossbones pirate flag, so the 'jolly' man of the flag is Roger.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name that follows 'Jolly' in the name of the pirate flag.

clue.text: Objects of baby's sneezes in the 28 scene

definitions.text: Objects of baby's sneezes in the 28 scene

parts.words: Objects of baby's sneezes in the 28 scene
parts.note: in the Duchess's kitchen the lullaby says the boy sneezes only to annoy and tease, so the aims of his sneezing are irritations

explanation.surface: Asks the purpose of a sneezing infant in the kitchen scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 is FLYING SAUCERS, the Duchess's kitchen in Alice; her song runs 'He only does it to annoy, Because he knows it teases.'
explanation.definitionFit: Irritations or nuisances, the things the sneezing child aims to cause.

clue.text: Many a ship's wrecked by such accidents

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number

indicators.note: wrecked means the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the word with its s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: Lots of vessels are wrecked through misadventures of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlucky incidents or misfortunes are mishaps.

clue.text: Swears atrociously about a point in the, solutions

indicators.note: about means the mangled letters go around the point
atrociously means the letters are badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone curses dreadfully about a detail in the solutions.
explanation.definitionFit: Replies to puzzles or questions are what solutions give.

clue.text: She is in the French fashion

indicators.note: in places is inside the French article

parts.note: la is a French word for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman is dressed in the French style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' completes the picture of 'in the French fashion'; the wordplay is IS inside LA.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, as in the Mona Lisa, stands for a female.

clue.text: Ousts workers who are inadequately supple

indicators.note: inadequately means the word falls short, its final letter missing

parts.note: taken as written
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Stiff employees are replaced by others.
explanation.definitionFit: To displace or take the place of someone is to oust them.

clue.text: Not the Quaker State

parts.note: Quakers are the Society of Friends, so a condition with no Friends is a state of having none

explanation.surface: Somewhere other than Pennsylvania, the Quaker State.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quaker State' is Pennsylvania's nickname, but 'State' is a condition, and Quakers are 'Friends'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no companions at all is a condition of loneliness.

clue.text: Music-maker is writing of living creatures

parts.note: an organ is an instrument that makes music
taken as written
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A musical instrument turns out to be a text about living beings.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants and animals are living things, each an individual life form.

clue.text: Excellent meal, if half-hearted

indicators.note: the heart of the meal word is a doubled letter, and losing half of that heart drops one of the pair

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A diner praises a dinner even though it was served without enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one P of the central PP from SUPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal terms of praise meaning very good or first-rate.

clue.text: Like the dance at the Teddy Bears' Picnic ?

definitions.text: Like the dance at the Teddy Bears' Picnic ?

parts.words: Like the dance at the Teddy Bears' Picnic ?
parts.note: teddy bears are covered in soft fur, and the Cornish town of Helston holds a spring festival dance with this very name

explanation.surface: A question about the sort of dance held at the toy bears' party in the song.
explanation.walkthrough: The Furry Dance is a traditional May dance through the streets of Helston in Cornwall; a dance of teddy bears would be fur-covered in the plain sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddy bears are soft and fur-covered, and the Helston May dance bears the same name.

clue.text: Maintain it will become mean with age

indicators.note: the clue says this word plus age makes mean, so taking age away from mean leaves the word wanted

parts.note: the average of a set of numbers is their mean
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims a person will grow stingy as the years pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it will become mean with age' says that adding AGE to the answer gives AVERAGE, a mean; 'mean' looks like 'stingy' but is the statistical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to assert or declare it firmly.

clue.text: East German XI returning to make one run

indicators.note: returning means the pieces are read backwards, as if coming home

parts.note: elf is the German word for eleven, the number written XI

explanation.surface: An East German football team travels home to play a single game.
explanation.walkthrough: XI looks like a football team, but it is the number eleven, ELF in German; E plus ELF, read back under 'returning', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away from danger is to take flight or escape.

clue.text: Wrong door into tatty NE club with first class cuisine

indicators.note: into puts the first jumble inside the second
tatty means shabby and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are set out incorrectly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone enters a run-down north-eastern club by the wrong door and finds excellent food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' makes ORDO from DOOR and 'tatty' makes C...NBLEU from NE CLUB; 'into' places ORDO after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: The French blue ribbon is a mark of top-quality cooking.

clue.text: Sends back a fellow amongst radicals

indicators.note: amongst places the fellow inside the word for radicals

parts.note: reds are left-wing radicals
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man is returned to the company of left-wing extremists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sends back' is the court's sense: a prisoner is sent back into custody to await trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that sends an accused person back into custody pending trial does exactly this.

clue.text: The emblem, an unusually pale flame.

indicators.note: unusually means the letters are put in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A badge shows a strangely pale fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The red leaf on a white ground is Canada's national symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada's national symbol, shown on its flag.

clue.text: Held in contempt for having made about one point only

indicators.note: about means the word for made goes around the point

parts.note: to score runs or goals is to make them, so made gives scored
a single compass point, N for north

explanation.surface: A player is despised for managing just a single point.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn someone is to regard them with disdain.

clue.text: Deal roughly with work-papers

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Someone handles work documents carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat people harshly or tyrannically is to keep them down by force.

clue.text: It sounds foolish to study this, element

indicators.note: it sounds says the words are spoken and the answer matches what is heard

parts.note: silly means foolish; to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: It seems foolish to study this element.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical element, the semiconductor basis of microchips.

clue.text: Is German in fashion ? Ask her

indicators.note: in places the German word inside the word for fashion

parts.note: mode means fashion or style
ist is the German word for is

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether German style is fashionable and is told to ask a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ask her' is a definition by example: the woman to consult about fashion is a maker of fashionable hats and gowns.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressmaker or milliner who makes fashionable clothes is the person to consult on style.

clue.text: Dial shows Fair for this child

definitions.text: Dial shows Fair for this child

parts.words: Dial shows Fair for this child
parts.note: dial is slang for face, and the nursery rhyme says the child born on a certain weekday is fair of face

explanation.surface: A clock face forecasts good weather for the child.
explanation.walkthrough: In the rhyme 'Monday's child is fair of face'; 'Dial' is slang for face, not a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The first weekday's child in the nursery rhyme is the one fair of face.

clue.text: As a Dickensian he takes the record

parts.note: taken as written
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A Dickens character takes the record.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is the fawning clerk in David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Uriah is the creepily humble clerk in Charles Dickens's David Copperfield.

clue.text: Dash out of the tunnel and whistle

indicators.note: out of means the letters are taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A train rushes out of the tunnel and blows its whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'tunnEL ANd'; 'Dash' is the noun for style and verve, not a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean flair, vigour and stylish energy.

clue.text: Cuts of the Devil

definitions.meaning: small cuts or notches in a surface
Old Nick is a name for the Devil

explanation.surface: Wounds inflicted by Satan.
explanation.definitionFit: Notches or small incisions; and the possessive of Old Nick, a nickname for Satan.

clue.text: Leave an eel without its tail

indicators.note: without its tail means the last letter of the eel is cut off

parts.note: a conger is a large sea eel

explanation.surface: Someone lets an eel go after cutting its tail off.
explanation.definitionFit: From French, a formal dismissal or permission to depart.

clue.text: Pale. but quiet in acquiescence

indicators.note: in places the call for quiet inside the word for yes

parts.note: ay is an old word for yes, a sign of agreement
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone pale but silent in agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey like ash, so drained of colour.

clue.text: East End's unusual requirements.

indicators.note: unusual means the letters appear in an uncommon order

parts.note: the word with its s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: London's East End has peculiar requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditionally working-class part of East London; here 'East' is just E.
explanation.definitionFit: Necessities or wants, the things one must have.

clue.text: Dare to change without the measure being reversed

indicators.note: without here means outside, so change goes around the reversed measure

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: being reversed means the measure word is read backwards

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: Someone dares to alter something without reversing the policy measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense 'outside': CHANGE wraps LLE, the reverse of ELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dare is an invitation to prove oneself, a provocation to act.

clue.text: Visitors from outer space in the Duchess's kitchen?

definitions.text: Visitors from outer space in the Duchess's kitchen?

parts.words: Visitors from outer space in the Duchess's kitchen?
parts.note: UFOs are read as crockery hurled through the air, as the cook does in the Duchess's kitchen in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Aliens land in an aristocrat's kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's Wonderland the Duchess's cook throws pans, plates and dishes at everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposed alien spacecraft have this name, and in the Alice scene real crockery literally flies.
